current.text: He is projected as a bench player. The projected Brooklyn starters are Mikel Brown Jr., Egor Demin, Michael Porter Jr., Julius Randle and Day'Ron Sharpe, and Clowney is in the second unit with Keon Ellis, Mo Wagner, Danny Wolf and Nolan Traore.
He faces a frontcourt logjam at the four with Julius Randle, Josh Minott and Danny Wolf.
Brooklyn did not give him a contract extension, so this is a pivotal season for him.
He is not a draft target. Experts say the Randle trade took away his fantasy value.
Brooklyn could give more minutes to young players like Clowney and Minott in the second half of the season, and Michael Porter Jr. could be traded.
Brooklyn does not own its draft pick and is projected to be one of the worst teams, with about 28 wins.
Brooklyn has 16 back-to-backs, tied for the most in the league. Its playoff schedule for a March 28 end is 3-4-3 games in weeks 19 to 21.

durable.text: He has been inconsistent, and his jump shot is unreliable. He has not been an efficient three-point shooter, although he has had hot stretches.
He shoots about 40% from the field, which is poor for a frontcourt player.
His rebounding, rim protection and defensive stats have been weak and inconsistent for a big.

note: Both sites value him at 0 USD (Yahoo rank 232, ESPN rank 269), and only 144 players get drafted, so leave him on waivers. He projects for about 40% FG on bench minutes and gives little in rebounds, steals or blocks for a big, so he does not fit any build. Early in the season, watch whether Brooklyn shifts minutes to its young players or trades Porter. A bigger role would make him a short-term waiver pickup for threes.
